newsitem.title: HONG KONG: New World aims for eight pct of HK's IDD traffic.
newsitem.headline: New World aims for eight pct of HK's IDD traffic.

text.p: New World Telephone, one of three new competitors to Hong Kong Telecommunications Ltd in the domestic market, on Tuesday said it aimed to capture eight percent of the territory's international phone traffic in the next five years.
Peter Tsang, chief executive of New World Telephone, said his company currently had around five percent of Hong Kong's international traffic after announcing a new service last year.

HongKong Telecom used to be the exclusive domestic and international provider in Hong Kong but lost its domestic fixed line monopoly last year. Aggressive new providers have been offering discount international calls on their domestic services.

Tsang said New World Telephone also aimed to snare seven percent of the local telephone service market, 15 percent of the personal communications service (PCS) mobile phone market and 18 percent of the multimedia market in the next five years.
"As a result, we are revising the forecast of our share of the overall telecommunications market to 9.5 percent from the originally envisaged five percent," Tsang said.
New World Telephone is a unit of New World Development Ltd. -- Hong Kong Newsroom (852) 2843 6441
